final_insights: Combining convolutional features with bidirectional recurrence produced the strongest recorded configuration in this study. The CNN condensed each image into eight ordered feature rows, allowing the LSTM to integrate spatial context. Architecture comparisons were consistent with the value of learned features, although unequal parameter counts limit attribution to recurrence alone.

The remaining classification difficulty was concentrated in visually similar animal categories. Cat and dog confusions accounted for 27 of 38 test errors, whereas several other classes were classified almost perfectly. This pattern shows why per-class evaluation and the confusion matrix provide information that overall accuracy alone cannot reveal about performance.

Validation scores varied across the tested regularization settings. Removing augmentation alone improved validation macro F1, and the combined removal of augmentation, dropout and weight decay achieved the highest validation score. The resulting gain establishes the selected configuration's performance on this split, while individual contributions remain unresolved without separate controlled experiments.
recommendations: Prioritize targeted evaluation of cat and dog errors using validation images. Examine object scale, occlusion, background composition and annotation ambiguity before comparing higher resolution, aspect-preserving resizing or targeted sampling. Retain class-specific precision, recall and F1 as evaluation criteria so that improvements in aggregate accuracy do not conceal weaker animal-class performance.

Use visually verified image groups when constructing future splits and reserve an independent holdout for final evaluation. Repeat experiments across multiple seeds and compare architectures under comparable parameter and tuning budgets. Vary augmentation, dropout and weight decay separately, selecting configurations through validation before inspecting test outcomes to strengthen experimental comparisons.

Assess practical efficiency alongside predictive quality by measuring inference latency, memory use and class-specific performance on representative images. Preserve configurations, split assignments, package versions, predictions and checkpoints for every experiment. Document active computation separately from elapsed duration, and evaluate whether a smaller CNN can achieve similar accuracy with fewer resources.
conclusion: This project demonstrated a complete workflow for classifying Natural Images with a CNN and LSTM, from image inspection and preprocessing through architecture design, training, tuning and evaluation. The validation-selected CNN-BiLSTM achieved 96.33% test accuracy and 0.9602 macro F1, correctly classifying 997 of 1,035 images. These findings meet the project's objective of implementing and evaluating an LSTM-based approach to spatial pattern analysis in still images.

Across the recorded experiments, the hybrid model provided a useful way to combine local convolutional features with ordered spatial information. The evaluation also identified animal-class discrimination as the main remaining challenge. The study therefore establishes a practical baseline for this dataset and training protocol. Further progress can build on this baseline through focused error analysis and independent, controlled evaluation of proposed improvements.
